newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says tight money policy to continue.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says tight money policy to continue.

text.p: Indonesian Central Bank Governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Tuesday the government will continue its tight money policy to contain speculative dollar buying in the foreign exchange market.
He told reporters Bank Indonesia had raised its short-term rates on Tuesday to help the rupiah.

"The monetary authority continues its tight policy. Since the government floated the rupiah, the rupiah has weakened on rising dollar demand from speculators and others. The demand causes the rupiah to fall," Djiwandono said.
Earlier on Tuesday, the bank raised rates for its bilateral certificates (SBIs) for maturities between one week and three months.
"We hope the substantial contraction (in liquidity) would help us to control movement of rupiah rates," Djiwandono said.
SBIs, used as a benchmark for interbank rates, are short-term rupiah-denominated obligations issued by the central bank to drain liquidity from the market.
The bank said rates for one-week bilateral SBIs were raised to 20 percent from 10.5, two to 22 percent from 11, one-month to 30 percent from 11.625 and three to 28 percent from 11.5 percent.
The bank maintained overnight SBIs at 15.0 percent, two- to six-day at 16.0 and six-month and one-year at 12.125 and 12.75 percent, respectively.
